title: The exit-5 conflict names a cause it has not established and never echoes the revision the caller sent
description:
Measured on dev (0.12.0) 2026-09-30 in a scratch workspace (mktemp + git init + quest init, never a live record), reproducing the lore-cli report against 0.11.0. The guard itself is correct; the conflict MESSAGE and its input are what cannot be trusted.

Positive control and finding, same invocation: sending the exact current revision exits 0. Empty string, deadbeef, the literal string null, and a genuinely stale revision all exit 5 with a byte-identical body whose input carries ONLY actualRevision -- the current revision -- and never the value that was sent. A sentinel string passed as the precondition appears 0 times anywhere in the error body.

Consequence, which is what makes this worse than merely unhelpful: the only revision in the error is the current one, so anyone who transcribes "the revision" out of it reproduces sent == actual exactly. That is how the original report arose.

Source: src/cli/main.ts:4173-4183 attaches only input.actualRevision. The sibling branch at src/cli/main.ts:4184-4201 (tracker_write_conflict, dependency_target_ambiguous, task_already_exists) emits the identical message with no input at all, so a caller cannot tell a failed precondition from another writer winning either.

Contributing trap from the same measurement: task create --json and task list --json carry no revision field at all (only task view does), so jq -r .data.revision prints null, and feeding that null to the precondition produces exactly this opaque exit 5.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A conflict whose sent revision never matched anything names the cause it established -- a mismatch between the sent value and the current revision -- instead of asserting the record changed concurrently
The conflict error carries the revision the caller sent beside actualRevision, so sent-versus-actual is a comparison the caller can make without reconstructing argv
A guarded-precondition failure is distinguishable from the revision-less conflicts (tracker_write_conflict, dependency_target_ambiguous, task_already_exists) that currently emit a byte-identical body
Verified against the built platform binary as well as the dev source, since the defect ships in the released CLI and reproduces on 0.11.0
